rv.q: There’s never a dull moment in the whole 70 minutes, and rarely have I felt myself so emotionally jostled in such a short time. ... Lane gives a tour-de-force performance that leaves your head spinning.
Though the play's overall structure requires a bit of clarifying, the means by which Lane reveals each low point in his life is something to behold.
Lane proves to be a remarkable actor and writer...that rare person who is willing to share how he went to hell—and why—and how he was able to come back to show us his heaven-sent gifts.
With those breakthroughs late in Triple Threat, Lane offers one of the most stirring epiphanies seen on stage in a while.
